description:
Show what a job pays, from the salaries in current WhatJobs listings: typical range, median, lowest and highest, plus a few listings with salaries.

Use this when the user asks how much a role pays or earns, salary ranges, or whether a salary is good, e.g. "How much does a nurse earn in Paris?" or "Data analyst salary in London".

Inputs:
- keyword: the job role only (e.g. "nurse", "software engineer").
- location: the place to search (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask for jobs near them. May be empty for the whole country.
- market: optional country code; if empty it is inferred from location. Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

Figures are in the country's own currency, for the pay period most listings use (per year in most countries, per month in some); the result says which. The result includes a link to all matching jobs on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.
name: get_salary_insights
title: Salary insights
